title: Stress, teamwork, adaptation, and resilience in couples with MS
summary: This study investigates the extent to which multiple sclerosis (MS)-related fatigue is associated with dyadic coping (joint coping with illness as a couple) and perceived stress. Individuals with a confirmed diagnosis of MS and their partners are eligible to participate. Participation is voluntary and involves completing online questionnaires as well as, optionally, providing a hair sample for the analysis of hair cortisol as a biomarker of stress. A total of 64 couples are planned for inclusion, and gift vouchers will be raffled as compensation for participation.

interventions.name: People with a confirmed diagnosis of multiple sclerosis (during an inpatient rehabilitation stay) will complete a one-time online questionnaire battery (including, e.g., the Dyadic Coping Inventory [DCI], Perceived Stress Scale [PSS], Trier Inventory for Chronic Stress [TICS], Brief Resilience Scale

criteria:
